name: Drypoint
summary: A way to scratch a line straight into a metal plate with a steel needle. The needle throws up a burr that prints a soft, velvet line.
how: Scratch the plate with a hard needle, held like a pencil; the burr stands on each side of the groove.
Print a small edition, because the burr wears down after 10 to 50 impressions.
Keep the line soft and dark where the burr is thick, and thin where it is not.
Combine it with etching or engraving when a crisp line is also needed.

origin.note: The Housebook Master, a south German artist, seems to have invented it; all his prints are in drypoint.

adoptions.via: Rembrandt prints The Three Crosses in heavy drypoint, with a thick burr in the dark areas.
Mary Cassatt shows colour prints in Paris that she makes with drypoint and aquatint.
